items.title: Noncommercial terms restrict use of the network and weights

findings.title: Noncommercial terms restrict use of the network and weights
findings.evidence:
SlimFormer++ Noncommercial Research License 1.0

This license applies only to copyrightable original contributions in this
repository whose rights are controlled by the SlimFormer++ copyright holders
(the "Licensors"). Third-party material is excluded and remains under its
original licenses. See NOTICE.md and licenses/Apache-2.0.txt.
findings.explanation: The module's core function needs the SlimFormer++ network (model.py) and downloaded weights, both under a noncommercial research license. The license permits redistribution, but the extension is advertised as Apache-2.0 in the module's acknowledgements and listed in a general-purpose index. Commercial users cannot use the segmentation output. This must be clearly communicated to users. Missing a referenced license file is a related defect.
findings.suggestion: State the noncommercial restriction in the catalog description and the module's help text (the disclaimer is currently about clinical use). Add the referenced licenses/Apache-2.0.txt or remove the reference. Confirm that the AMOS2022 training-data terms do not restrict redistribution of derived weights.

items.title: Silent pip install into Slicer's shared environment on segmentation

findings.title: Silent pip install into Slicer's shared environment on segmentation
findings.evidence:
if numpyVersion < Version("2") and pandasVersion >= Version("3.1"):
    self.status("Installing Python packages (this may take several minutes) ...", cancellable=False)
    self.log(f"Installing a pandas version that works with numpy {numpyVersion} ...")
    slicer.util.pip_install("pandas<3.1")
findings.explanation: _ensurePandasMatchesNumpy runs on every segmentation when numpy<2 and pandas>=3.1 are detected. It then calls slicer.util.pip_install without asking the user, changing a package that Slicer and other extensions may use. The user is only asked to confirm the nnU-Net/PyTorch installation, not this downgrade. The pandas pin is also outside the stated install-confirmation flow.
findings.suggestion: Ask for explicit confirmation before any pip install (as is done for the main requirements), or remove the pin and document the macOS numpy/pandas issue. Confirm whether pandas is bundled with Slicer, and if so avoid downgrading it.

items.title: Catalog pins a mutable branch, not a reviewed commit

findings.title: Catalog pins a mutable branch, not a reviewed commit
findings.explanation: scm_revision is 'main', so the code a user gets can change without a catalog update. The reviewed commit e9b486ccec53b9edabd3d06d8c93efd42859b421 is not what the index builds. This is a reproducibility and review-baseline issue, not a defect in the code itself.
findings.suggestion: Set scm_revision to a specific commit (or a release tag) that was reviewed.

findings.title: Network download has no timeout
findings.evidence: with urllib.request.urlopen(model["url"]) as response, open(zipPath, "wb") as out:
findings.explanation: urllib.request.urlopen is called without a timeout, so a stalled connection can block the segmentation thread indefinitely. Cancellation is checked only between reads, so a stall in read() is not interruptible.
findings.suggestion: Pass timeout=... to urlopen and handle timeouts as download errors.

items.title: SHA256SUMS entries are joined to the staging path without validation

findings.title: SHA256SUMS entries are joined to the staging path without validation
findings.explanation: Entries in SHA256SUMS are read and joined to the staging directory with no check for absolute paths or '..'. Only a file hash is read, so the impact is limited to reading files the user can already read. The archive's own member names are validated, so this is defense-in-depth.
findings.suggestion: Reject names that are absolute or contain '..' before hashing, as is done for archive members.
